quote.text:
Two of the three most expensive mistakes in production AI systems are invisible until they are not.

Researchers at IIT analyzed 150 real production incidents from open-source and enterprise compound AI systems and catalogued 23 failure modes. None of them happen inside the model. They happen at the boundaries, where one component hands off to the next.

The numbers that should worry you: circuit breakers cut cascade propagation by 89%. Output quality gates catch 73% of silent degradation before a user ever sees it. Systems that stack three or more resilience patterns cut mean time to recovery by 71%.

Here is the part most teams will miss. They will read this as a model problem, a prompt problem, an eval problem. It is none of those. A model can be perfect and the system still fails, because the failure lives in the handoff. Retrieval, generation, tool, orchestration, integration. Each boundary is where reliability dies quietly.

This is exactly what the agent reliability gap is, measured at last. The model is not the unit of risk. The pipeline is. If you are running agent workflows in production, the question to ask is not which model is smarter. It is which boundaries have a circuit breaker, and which ones are just hope.

#AI #Agents #AIOperations
